Mental Health Care Plan

- Referring GP: Dr. Smith, Practice: Babylon, [Practice Address not recorded]. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Anxiety symptoms (work-related, generalized, sleep disruption, physiological symptoms)
- Secondary: Low mood/depressive symptoms
- Tertiary: Palpitations/physiological symptoms associated with anxiety

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: Not recorded
- Allergies/ADRs: Not recorded
- Past Medical History: Not recorded

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: Not recorded
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): None reported; no previous therapy or psychiatric treatment
- Family History: Mother with past depression

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Lives with parents
- Social Support: Good support system (family, especially mother)
- Occupation/Education: Works in head office team for fashion retailer (new job in unfamiliar sector; stressful work environment; has never worked in retail before)
- Alcohol Use: Drinks alcohol; higher intake on Fridays/Saturdays (often over recommended limits); occasional wine during the week
- Smoking/Substance Use: Smokes occasionally; does not use drugs
- Key Stressors: New, stressful job; unsupportive supervisor; impact on enjoyment of previous activities; difficulty relaxing

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Not recorded
- Mood & Affect: Anxious, distressed, low mood, decreased enjoyment (anhedonia), tense
- Speech & Thought: Not recorded
- Perception: No reports of hallucinations, paranoia, or perceptual disturbance

Cognition:
- Orientation: Not recorded
- Attention/Concentration: Not directly assessed; impaired by poor sleep and anxiety (implied)
- Memory: Not recorded
- Insight & Judgement: Aware of symptoms; seeking help appropriately

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Significantly reduced (3–4 hours/night), poor sleep quality, difficulty falling asleep, waking early with palpitations/anxiety
- Appetite: No significant changes; increased chocolate consumption reported
- Motivation/Energy: Markedly decreased energy, lack of enjoyment in activities, finds it difficult to motivate herself
- Anxiety Symptoms: Prominent; racing heart, morning dread, palpitations, worry about work performance, physiological arousal, avoidance of enjoyable activities, tension related to work and public transport

Risk Assessment
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: Denies any suicidal ideation or self-harm; no risk to others
- Protective Factors: Good family support, insight into problems, motivation to seek help, living with parents, no current intent or plans of harm
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Low
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation
Valerie Cole presents with a two-month history of escalating anxiety and low mood, closely related to starting a new, stressful job with an unsupportive supervisor. Symptoms include work-related anticipatory anxiety, palpitations, sleep disturbance, low energy, and anhedonia. She retains insight, reports protective factors (supportive family, especially mother with lived experience), and no history of previous mental health issues. There are no risk concerns at present. Stressors are mainly occupational and environmental, exacerbated by reduced social engagement and poor sleep.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Anxiety symptoms (work-related)
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce work-related anxiety; regain ability to enjoy daily activities; improve sleep and coping
- Clinical Goal(s): Alleviate symptoms of anxiety; address stressors and physiological symptoms; support occupational functioning
- Actions (Patient): 
  - Access one-to-one therapy (self-referral advised)
  - Use suggested online resources for anxiety management and sleep hygiene
  - Monitor and report on impact of interventions and symptom changes
  - Arrange for blood tests as discussed
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide information/link for NHS talking therapies (CBT-based)
  - Supply online resources for anxiety and sleep
  - Document information for sleep improvement
  - Order blood tests to rule out physical causes of palpitations
  - Arrange follow-up appointment after blood test results are available

Secondary Problem: Low mood/depressive symptoms
- Patient Goal(s): Regain enjoyment in activities; increase energy and motivation
- Clinical Goal(s): Improve mood and functioning; monitor for depression
- Actions (Patient):
  - Engage in therapy as above
  - Reintroduce enjoyable activities as able
  - Seek support from family/friends as needed
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Monitor mood changes at follow-up
  - Provide education on early signs of depression and coping strategies

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Anxiety, sleep hygiene, online resources, talking therapies, warning signs of worsening symptoms
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased anxiety, further sleep disruption, reduced ability to attend work or perform daily activities, mood deterioration, withdrawal from social contacts
- Coping Strategies: Access family support, use therapy/online interventions, sleep hygiene, gradual re-engagement with enjoyable/rewarding activities, maintain communication with healthcare provider

Consent, Coordination & Review
- Patient Consent to Plan: Not explicitly recorded
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently; planned referral for talking therapy
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: After blood test results and following therapy referral (timeline not specified)
